008package paint.viewer.ui;
009
010import paint.shared.utils.PaintLogger;
011import paint.shared.utils.PaintPrefs;
012import paint.viewer.model.RecordingEntry;
013import paint.viewer.io.TiffMoviePlayer;
014import paint.viewer.ui.frames.ViewerFrame;
015
016import javax.swing.*;
017import java.awt.*;
018import java.nio.file.Files;
019import java.nio.file.Path;
020
021/**
022 * Controller responsible for playing ND2/TIFF recordings and keeping the PAINT Viewer
023 * UI in a consistent state during playback.
024 *
025 * <p>This class prevents concurrent playback, disables the entire ViewerFrame UI while a
026 * recording plays, and re-enables it as soon as the player window closes.</p>
027 *
028 * <p>Use {@link #playRecording(RecordingEntry)} to start playback.</p>
029 */
030public final class RecordingPlaybackController {
031
032    private final ViewerFrame frame;
033    private volatile boolean playing = false;
034
035    /**
036     * Creates a new Playback Controller bound to a given {@link ViewerFrame}.
037     *
038     * @param frame the viewer frame whose UI will be disabled/enabled during playback
039     */
040    public RecordingPlaybackController(ViewerFrame frame) {
041        this.frame = frame;
042    }
043
044    /**
045     * @return {@code true} if a playback session is currently active.
046     */
047    public boolean isPlaying() {
048        return playing;
049    }
050
051    /**
052     * Starts playback of the given recording. This method:
053     *
054     * <ol>
055     *   <li>Beeps and returns if a recording is already playing.</li>
056     *   <li>Resolves the recording's image file under the project's Images Root.</li>
057     *   <li>Disables the ViewerFrame UI and opens the player.</li>
058     *   <li>Re-enables the UI when the player window closes, or if loading fails.</li>
059     * </ol>
060     *
061     * <p>Returns as soon as the player has been started; playback itself is asynchronous.</p>
062     *
063     * @param entry the recording to play
064     */
065    public void playRecording(RecordingEntry entry) {
066        if (playing) {
067            Toolkit.getDefaultToolkit().beep();
068            return;
069        }
070
071        // Hide info popup before playback begins
072        frame.getLeftGridPanel().hideSquareInfoIfVisible();
073
074        // Determine the images root directory
075        Path imagesRoot = frame.getProject().getImagesRootPath();
076        if (imagesRoot == null) {
077            String stored = PaintPrefs.getString("Path", "Images Root", "");
078            if (stored != null && !stored.isEmpty()) {
079                imagesRoot = Path.of(stored);
080            } else {
081                JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(
082                        frame,
083                        "No Images Root is defined.\nPlease set it in the Project Specification dialog.",
084                        "Configuration Error",
085                        JOptionPane.ERROR_MESSAGE
086                );
087                return;
088            }
089        }
090
091        String experimentName = entry.getExperimentName();
092        String recordingName  = entry.getRecordingName();
093
094        // Build full ND2/TIFF path
095        Path imagePath = imagesRoot.resolve(experimentName).resolve(recordingName + ".nd2");
096        if (!Files.exists(imagePath)) {
097            JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(
098                    frame,
099                    "Recording file not found:\n" + imagePath,
100                    "File Missing",
101                    JOptionPane.ERROR_MESSAGE
102            );
103            return;
104        }
105
106        // The file can exist and still not be readable. On macOS the images usually live on an
107        // external drive, and access to removable volumes is gated: the file is visible, but
108        // opening it fails with "Operation not permitted". Say so here, rather than letting the
109        // image loader report it as an obscure Bio-Formats failure.
110        if (!Files.isReadable(imagePath)) {
111            PaintLogger.errorf("Not permitted to read %s", imagePath);
112            JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(
113                    frame,
114                    "The recording exists but cannot be read:\n" + imagePath
115                            + "\n\nIf it is on an external drive, macOS may be blocking access."
116                            + "\nGrant the application access under System Settings > Privacy &"
117                            + " Security > Files and Folders (Removable Volumes), or Full Disk"
118                            + " Access, and restart it.",
119                    "Cannot Read Recording",
120                    JOptionPane.ERROR_MESSAGE
121            );
122            return;
123        }
124
125        // Mark playback active and disable the viewer UI. TiffMoviePlayer calls us back on the
126        // EDT when its window closes (or immediately if the file cannot be loaded), so the UI
127        // is always re-enabled exactly once.
128        //
129        // This used to work by polling Window.getWindows() for up to 10 seconds looking for a
130        // window whose title equalled the *file name*. TiffMoviePlayer titles its window
131        // "Movie Player - <file name>", so the match never succeeded: the viewer sat disabled
132        // for the full 10 s of polling, the close listeners were never attached, and the UI was
133        // only restored by the fall-through at the end.
134        playing = true;
135        frame.disableUI();
136
137        try {
138            new TiffMoviePlayer().playMovie(imagePath.toString(), () -> {
139                playing = false;
140                frame.enableUI();
141            });
142        } catch (RuntimeException ex) {
143            // playMovie only *starts* playback, so this catches a failure to launch, not a
144            // playback error. Re-enable the UI: no callback is coming.
145            playing = false;
146            frame.enableUI();
147            PaintLogger.error("Could not start movie playback", ex);
148            JOptionPane.showMessageDialog(
149                    frame,
150                    "Movie playback error:\n" + ex.getMessage(),
151                    "Playback Error",
152                    JOptionPane.ERROR_MESSAGE
153            );
154        }
155    }
156}
